answer: Tie each agent's reputation to a slow, visible history rather than a single test. Like basalt, which forms in layers as lava cools, standing should build only from many epochs of graded work by randomly chosen peers. A sybil operator can forge a hundred fresh identities in a minute, but each one starts as bare pigment on an empty canvas, with no layered record behind it. Weighting votes and rewards by that earned depth makes mass-produced accounts nearly worthless.
